answer.generated: Vertical partitioning divides an entity into subentities based on attributes, resulting in smaller entities that can be stored more efficiently. This approach enables faster data retrieval because each partition contains fewer attributes, allowing a single access to obtain much data. In contrast, horizontal partitioning splits entities into subsets based on rows, which may require multiple accesses to gather all relevant data. The key difference lies in attribute distribution versus row distribution, with vertical partitioning optimizing for attribute-based queries by reducing the size of individual partitions.
